name: Pyrewood Chapel
summary: Pyrewood Chapel is a modest house of worship standing near the entrance of Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine Forest. In earlier days this site served as the community's town hall, where local leadership gathered under the watchful eyes of Forsaken infiltrators. Today, it stands as a solemn reflection of a village cursed by dark magics every time the sun sets.

sections.title: From Council to Church
sections.body: Situated near the approach to Pyrewood Village, this stone structure long served as the municipal heart of the settlement—the Pyrewood Town Hall. It was within those civic walls that the council met, entirely unaware that agents of the Forsaken, like Deathstalker Faerleia, lurked in the rafters plotting their demise. Though remodeled into a chapel, it remains tied to the eerie, double-lived existence of Pyrewood, where human residents cling to faith by day and surrender to feral beastliness by night.

faq.answer: Pyrewood Chapel stands near the entrance of Pyrewood Village, in the southern reaches of Silverpine Forest not far from the Greymane Wall.

faq.q: Was this building always a chapel?
faq.answer: Historically, the structure served as the Pyrewood Town Hall. The village council conducted civic affairs there before the site became designated as the village chapel.

faq.q: What interest do the Forsaken have in this building?
faq.answer: Pyrewood's leadership and strategic location near Shadowfang Keep have made it an ongoing target for the Undercity. Deathstalkers, such as Faerleia, have targeted the hall to spy on and ambush the town's ruling council.

faq.q: What happens to the villagers inside at night?
faq.answer: Like the rest of Pyrewood Village, any residents seeking solace in the chapel succumb to the local curse at sundown, transforming from peaceful humans into savage worgen.

angles.text: The Forsaken keep a close eye on Pyrewood's community buildings to eliminate local leaders and exploit the strange affliction plaguing the villagers.
The chapel represents a desperate human effort to maintain Holy Light worship on the edges of Silverpine, though faith offers little protection against the village's nocturnal affliction.
